compiled_by: Claude (AI co-editor), first pass from official pages read through WebFetch on 2026-10-16; numbers marked 'read twice' were re-read in a second, narrower fetch of the same page or found in a second source, as each source's note says. Members are the substances that the EUDA, the DEA and NIDA pages read actually name. Not yet checked by a second reader or by the senior author.

synonyms: inhalants (EUDA, which notes the group is defined by route of administration; DEA; NIDA)
alkyl nitrites, or 'poppers' (EUDA: a subgroup of volatile substances)
volatile solvents, gases, aerosols and nitrites (the four types of inhalants in the NIDA bulletin)

members.name: Amyl nitrite (isoamyl nitrite)
members.iupac: Nitrous acid, 3-methylbutyl ester (CAS index name, NIST); 3-Methylbutyl nitrite (among NIST's other names)
cas: 110-46-3: amyl nitrite, a mixture of isomers, chiefly isoamyl nitrite (EUDA, read twice); isoamyl nitrite (NIST, read twice)
members.note: EUDA: the only nitrite with a medical use (cyanide antidote), and also sold as 'poppers'. NIDA names amyl nitrite among the nitrites.

members.name: n-Butyl nitrite
members.iupac: Nitrous acid, butyl ester (CAS index name, NIST)
cas: 544-16-1: n-butyl nitrite (EUDA, read twice; NIST, read twice)
members.note: EUDA: poppers usually contain butyl or isobutyl nitrite. NIDA: most poppers contain isobutyl nitrite or butyl nitrite.

members.name: Isobutyl nitrite
members.iupac: Nitrous acid, 2-methylpropyl ester (CAS index name, NIST)
cas: 542-56-3: isobutyl nitrite (EUDA, read twice; NIST, read twice)
members.note: Isobutyl and n-butyl nitrite share the formula C4H9NO2 (NIST).

members.name: Isopropyl nitrite
cas: 541-42-4: isopropyl nitrite (EUDA, read twice; NIST, read twice, where the record is named 'iso-Propyl nitrite')
members.note: Named by EUDA as a 'poppers' nitrite.

members.name: Cyclohexyl nitrite
members.iupac: Nitrous acid, cyclohexyl ester (NIST record name)
cas: 5156-40-1: cyclohexyl nitrite (NIST, read twice)
members.note: Named by NIDA among the nitrites; not in the EUDA table.

members.name: Butane
cas: 106-97-8: butane (NIST, read twice); the EUDA table gives this number for its row 'Butane, iso-butane, propane, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG)' (read twice)

members.name: Isobutane

members.name: Propane
cas: 74-98-6: propane (NIST, read twice)
members.note: Named by EUDA (in the butane row, with no separate CAS number), the DEA and NIDA (propane from gas grills).

members.name: Dimethyl ether
cas: 115-10-6: dimethyl ether (EUDA, read twice; NIST, read twice)
members.note: EUDA: a propellant.

members.note: Covered on its own page (nitrous-oxide), where its formula and molar mass are given. Named by EUDA (propellant, analgesic, anaesthetic), the DEA (in balloons) and NIDA (among medical anaesthetic gases).

cas: 108-88-3: toluene (EUDA, read twice; NIST, read twice)
members.note: EUDA: in paint thinners and glues. Not named on the DEA or NIDA pages read.

members.note: EUDA: in paint thinners and glues.

members.note: A mixture, so EUDA gives no CAS number. EUDA: automotive fuel, reformulated in Australia to be low in aromatics to minimise misuse. NIDA lists gasoline among volatile solvents.

cas: 60-29-7: diethyl ether (EUDA, read twice; NIST, read twice, where the record is named 'Ethyl ether')
members.note: EUDA: a solvent, car starter and redundant anaesthetic. NIDA lists ether among medical anaesthetic gases.

members.name: Chloroform

members.note: EUDA: a solvent and redundant anaesthetic. NIDA lists chloroform among medical anaesthetic gases.

cas: 151-67-7: halothane (EUDA, under the name Fluothane, read twice; NIST, read twice)

forms.detail: Domestic, industrial or medicinal products: spray deodorants, glue, lighter refills, spray air fresheners, party-balloon helium cylinders and automotive fuel; aerosols, which contain a high proportion of propellant (deodorants and antiperspirants, hair spray, air freshener, paint); liquefied petroleum gas (LPG).

Volatile solvents: paint thinners and removers, dry-cleaning fluids, degreasers, gasoline, glues, correction fluids, felt-tip marker fluids and electronic contact cleaners. Gases: butane lighters, propane gas grills, cooling-system fluids, and the medical anaesthetic gases ether, chloroform, halothane and nitrous oxide. Aerosols: spray paint, hair sprays, deodorant sprays, whipped cream dispensers, fabric protector sprays and vegetable oil cooking sprays.

forms.form: Products named by the DEA (United States)
forms.detail: Typewriter correction fluid, air-conditioning refrigerant, felt-tip and highlighter markers, spray paint, air freshener, butane, cooking spray, glue, lighter fluid, cleaning fluids, paint and paint thinner; nitrous oxide in balloons.

EUDA: usually butyl or isobutyl nitrite, often impure, sold in small glass bottles with suggestive names. NIDA: most contain isobutyl nitrite or butyl nitrite and are sold in small brown bottles labelled 'video head cleaner', 'room odorizer', 'leather cleaner' or 'liquid aroma'.
WHO ATC lists amyl nitrite among antidotes (V03AB22); EUDA: a cyanide antidote.
